title: Sarvajan Pension Yojana Jharkhand: Rs 1,000/Month Apply
meta_description: Sarvajan Pension Yojana Jharkhand gives Rs 1,000/month to elderly (60+), widows, destitute women, disabled, PVTG and HIV/AIDS patients. Apply at Block office.

hero.one_liner: Sarvajan Pension Yojana gives Rs 1,000 a month to the elderly, widows, and people with disabilities in Jharkhand. A universal pension, no BPL card needed.

what_is_it: Sarvajan Pension Yojana (SPY) is Jharkhand's universal social pension scheme, providing a monthly Rs 1,000 to eligible senior citizens, widows, destitute women, persons with disabilities, members of Primitive Tribal Groups (PVTGs), and people living with HIV/AIDS. The word Sarvajan means 'for all people' in Sanskrit/Hindi, and the scheme reflects the state government's intent to extend pension coverage beyond the typical old-age category to include multiple vulnerable groups.

The scheme is implemented by the Department of Women, Child Development and Social Security (DWCDSS) of the Jharkhand state government. This departmental assignment reflects the scheme's character as a social protection measure rather than a retirement pension, covering several categories of people who need income support not because they have retired but because they are in vulnerable life situations.

eligibility_filters.notes: Jharkhand residents aged 60+ for old age, plus widows and persons with disabilities. Rs 1,000 a month by the 5th via DBT. Universal, no BPL card needed, only non-taxpayers. Apply at the Block office or Aapke Dwar camp. Annual life certificate required.

how_to_apply.title: Identify your category
how_to_apply.description: Confirm which Sarvajan Pension category you fall under: old age (60+), widow (any age), destitute woman (18+), disabled (5+), PVTG member, or HIV/AIDS patient. Gather documents relevant to your category: Aadhaar card, age proof, death certificate of spouse (widow), disability certificate (disabled), ART certificate (HIV/AIDS), tribe certificate (PVTG), bank passbook.

how_to_apply.title: Visit BDO or Circle Officer
how_to_apply.description: Go to the Block Development Officer's office (rural) or Circle Officer's office (urban). Collect the Sarvajan Pension Yojana application form, fill in all details accurately, attach photocopies of required documents, and submit the completed form at the counter.

how_to_apply.title: Field verification
how_to_apply.description: After submission, a government functionary conducts a field visit to verify your eligibility (age, widowhood, disability, or destitute status). Ensure you are available at your stated address, as the field visit is usually completed within 2-4 weeks of submission.

how_to_apply.title: Approval and enrolment
how_to_apply.description: Once verified and approved, your name is added to the Sarvajan Pension beneficiary list and your bank account is registered in the DBT system; you will receive an acknowledgement from the BDO or Circle Officer's office confirming enrolment. Processing typically takes 30-60 days from application to first payment.

how_to_apply.title: Receive Rs 1,000 by the 5th of each month
how_to_apply.description: Once enrolled, Rs 1,000 is credited to your Aadhaar-linked bank account by the 5th of every month; check your passbook or mobile banking app to confirm each monthly credit. If a payment is missed, contact your BDO office or the DWCDSS helpline for assistance.

ministry: Department of Women, Child Development and Social Security, Jharkhand

extra_sections.heading: What Sarvajan Pension Yojana Is
content: The pension amount under Sarvajan Pension Yojana is Rs 1,000 per month per beneficiary, disbursed by the 5th of every month via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to the beneficiary's Aadhaar-linked bank account. The DBT mechanism reduces the scope for leakage and ensures that the pension arrives directly and on time each month.

For the old-age category, beneficiaries must be at least 60 years of age and a resident of Jharkhand; there is no upper age ceiling, so even centenarians receive the pension. The old-age component integrates with the central IGNOAPS (Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme), which also pays Rs 200-500 per month, and Sarvajan effectively tops up the central pension to Rs 1,000.

Widows of any age who are resident in Jharkhand are eligible under the widow category of Sarvajan Pension, with proof of widowhood such as the husband's death certificate, a court order, or a Gram Panchayat certificate. There is no income ceiling for widows, making the pension accessible to all widowed Jharkhand women irrespective of their financial status.

Destitute women aged 18 years and above form a distinct eligible category under Sarvajan Pension, separate from the widow category, covering women who have been abandoned or have no means of support. A destitute woman's status is certified by the Gram Panchayat or ward office, and this category provides a safety net for economically abandoned women who are not widows.

extra_sections.heading: Who Can Get the Pension
content: Persons with disabilities aged 5 years and above are eligible under the disability category, with the disability (at 40% or above as per the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act) certified by a government medical officer. This is one of the few social pension schemes in India where the minimum age for the disability category is as low as 5 years, ensuring even disabled children can receive support.

Members of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) in Jharkhand such as the Birhor, Asur, Sauriya Paharia, Korwa, and Mal Paharia are eligible for Sarvajan Pension regardless of age, recognising the extreme vulnerability and marginalization of these communities. This PVTG category reflects Jharkhand's unique tribal demography and the state's commitment to providing a basic income floor to its most marginalised indigenous groups.

extra_sections.title: A Universal Pension, Not Just for BPL
extra_sections.content:
Sarvajan Pension gives Rs 1,000 a month to the elderly, widows, and people with disabilities in Jharkhand. The word Sarvajan means for all.

Unlike older pension schemes, it does not need a BPL card. Anyone who meets the age or category rule and is not a taxpayer can apply.

extra_sections.heading: Who Can Get the Pension More
content: People living with HIV/AIDS are the sixth category under Sarvajan Pension Yojana, with eligibility confirmed through a medical certificate from an Anti-Retroviral Therapy (ART) centre or government hospital. This inclusion is significant because HIV/AIDS often prevents individuals from maintaining regular employment, and the monthly pension provides both financial support and a degree of social recognition for the health challenges these individuals face.

To apply for Sarvajan Pension Yojana, applicants in rural areas should approach the Block Development Officer (BDO) at the block-level office, while applicants in urban areas should contact the Circle Officer (CO) at the circle office. The application form is available at these offices, and submission is offline; there is no fully online application portal for Sarvajan Pension at the state level.

extra_sections.heading: The Different Categories
content: Documents required for the Sarvajan Pension Yojana application vary by category but generally include the Aadhaar card, age proof (for old-age category), death certificate of husband (for widows), disability certificate from a government medical officer (for disabled), caste/tribe certificate (for PVTG), ART centre certificate (for HIV/AIDS), proof of Jharkhand residency, and bank account passbook for DBT linkage.

After the BDO or Circle Officer receives the application, a field verification is conducted to confirm eligibility, and once approved, the applicant is added to the beneficiary list and begins receiving Rs 1,000 per month. The processing time varies by block but is typically 30 to 60 days from application to first payment.

The Jharkhand Sarvajan Pension Yojana is closely aligned with the central government's National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP), which includes the IGNOAPS (old age), IGNWPS (widow), and IGNDPS (disability) pension components. The central scheme typically provides Rs 200-500 per month, and Jharkhand's Sarvajan Pension tops up this amount to reach Rs 1,000 per month for covered beneficiaries.

Beneficiaries who are already receiving the central IGNOAPS or IGNWPS pension are often simultaneously enrolled in Sarvajan Pension to receive the top-up, so the total pension received can be the sum of both components. Families of elderly or disabled individuals should check with their BDO whether their relative is receiving both the central and state pension components or only one.

extra_sections.heading: How to Apply
content: The Aadhaar-linked bank account requirement for Sarvajan Pension means that beneficiaries who do not have a bank account or whose account is not Aadhaar-seeded may face delays in receiving payments. The state government has conducted Aadhaar-bank linkage camps in tribal and remote areas to address this barrier, particularly for elderly beneficiaries who may find it difficult to visit a bank independently.

Social audit of the Sarvajan Pension beneficiary list is conducted periodically by the Gram Sabha and the Jharkhand government's Social Audit Unit, allowing community members to raise objections against ineligible inclusions and flag eligible persons who have been excluded. This participatory monitoring keeps pension rolls accurate and prevents ghost beneficiaries.

The disability pension component of Sarvajan Pension has become increasingly important in the context of Jharkhand's industrial and mining sectors, which have higher-than-average rates of occupational disability. Workers who develop mining-related or industrial disabilities and lose their ability to work can apply for the disability pension as a source of income support, even if they are below the old-age threshold.

Sarvajan Pension Yojana beneficiaries who move from one block to another within Jharkhand need to transfer their pension to the new block's records by informing the new BDO and submitting a transfer request. The pension is linked to the individual's Aadhaar and can follow the beneficiary across blocks without requiring a fresh application, although processing at the new block may take some weeks.

extra_sections.heading: How and When You Are Paid
content: For elderly beneficiaries above 80 years of age, the central IGNOAPS provides Rs 500 per month (as against Rs 200 for those between 60 and 79), and combined with the Sarvajan top-up, the total pension for the oldest and most vulnerable senior citizens in Jharkhand can reach Rs 1,500 per month. This enhanced support for the oldest age group is designed to address the reality that healthcare costs and physical limitations increase with extreme old age.

The Jharkhand government has periodically revised Sarvajan Pension amounts upward, reflecting inflation and increasing cost of living. While the base rate has been Rs 1,000 per month in recent years, the state budget presentations have included provisions for periodic revision of this amount, and beneficiaries and advocacy groups have called for an increase to at least Rs 1,500-2,000 per month to keep pace with inflation in food and medicines.

extra_sections.title: Paid Early Each Month
extra_sections.desc:
The pension is credited by the 5th of every month, straight to the beneficiary's bank account by DBT.

Keep your Aadhaar seeded to the bank, and submit your annual life certificate so the pension does not stop.

extra_sections.heading: How and When You Are Paid More
content: In many rural Jharkhand households, the Rs 1,000 Sarvajan Pension received by an elderly grandparent or disabled family member represents the only reliable monthly income for the entire household, particularly in families where working-age members are engaged in uncertain agricultural or daily-wage labour. The pension thus functions not just as individual support but as a household income anchor for the poorest families.

Women who are both widowed and elderly (above 60 years) may technically qualify under both the widow category and the old-age category of Sarvajan Pension, but they are typically enrolled under just one category in the system. In such cases, the BDO's office usually processes the application under whichever category was applied for first; applicants are encouraged to clarify which category is being used during their visit to the BDO office.

extra_sections.heading: The Annual Life Certificate
content: The Sarvajan Pension Yojana beneficiary database in Jharkhand is maintained digitally at the state level and can be updated at the block level. If a beneficiary's bank account changes (for example, due to branch transfer or account closure), they must immediately inform the BDO office so that the DBT linkage can be updated; pension payments to a closed account will fail and may need to be recovered through a fresh payment request.

Jharkhand's Sarvajan Pension Yojana is broader in coverage than the central NSAP (National Social Assistance Programme) in one key respect: it does not impose income or BPL card requirements for all categories. While NSAP typically requires BPL status for many of its pension components, Sarvajan Pension's widow and destitute woman categories do not require a BPL card, making these categories more accessible to women who may not have obtained a poverty card.

extra_sections.title: Pension Stopped Suddenly?
extra_sections.content:
The most common reasons are a missed annual life certificate or a broken Aadhaar-bank link. Both are fixable.

Submit your life certificate, re-seed your Aadhaar if needed, and contact the Block office with your pension number to restart it.

extra_sections.heading: The Annual Life Certificate More
content: For applicants who face language barriers (particularly in tribal-dominated districts where Santali, Mundari, or Ho languages are spoken as the primary tongue), the Gram Panchayat-level awareness drives for Sarvajan Pension Yojana are often conducted in local tribal languages with the help of community liaisons. The block-level application form can be filled in Hindi or English, but the BDO staff typically assist non-literate applicants in completing the form.

The Jharkhand government has implemented a life certificate requirement for continuing Sarvajan Pension beneficiaries: elderly and disabled pensioners must submit a Jeevan Praman (digital life certificate) once a year to confirm that they are still alive and eligible. This can be done at Aadhaar-enabled banking points, Common Service Centres, or post offices, and failure to submit a life certificate on time can result in pension payments being temporarily suspended until the certificate is provided.

extra_sections.heading: If the Pension Stops
content: For persons with disabilities, the Sarvajan Pension Yojana serves an especially important function because disability often coincides with reduced earning capacity, and many disabled individuals in Jharkhand are unable to pursue regular employment in agriculture or labour markets. The Rs 1,000 monthly pension does not replace a full income but provides a floor that, combined with family support and other welfare entitlements, can meaningfully improve the disabled individual's quality of life.

Jharkhand's tribal communities, particularly those in the Kolhan region (West Singhbhum) and Santhal Parganas (Dumka, Sahebganj, Pakur), have high rates of elderly residents who live in poverty after a lifetime of agricultural or forest-based livelihoods. For these elderly tribal residents, the Sarvajan Pension represents a form of old-age income security that their occupational history (unlike formal sector workers) would never have generated through provident funds or gratuity.

extra_sections.heading: If the Pension Stops More
content: Awareness about Sarvajan Pension Yojana is spread through Gram Sabhas, ASHA workers, Anganwadi centres, and the network of Common Service Centres (CSCs) across Jharkhand's blocks. Periodic beneficiary drives are held to identify uncovered eligible persons, particularly elderly individuals living alone, isolated widows, and disabled children in remote areas who may not be aware of their entitlement to the monthly Rs 1,000 pension.

The convergence of Sarvajan Pension with the Abua Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (Rs 15 lakh health cover) and the Maiya Samman Yojana (Rs 2,500/month for eligible women) creates a comprehensive social protection package for vulnerable women in Jharkhand. A widow below 50 years may receive both Maiya Samman and the Sarvajan widow pension simultaneously, and adding the Abua Swasthya health cover means she has income support, health coverage, and potentially housing assistance under Abua Awas as well.

extra_sections.title: Why the Scheme Matters Notes
extra_sections.content:
Jharkhand has one of the largest PVTG populations in India, and the decision to include PVTG members in Sarvajan Pension without any age restriction reflects the government's recognition that Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups face systemic economic disadvantages that cannot be adequately addressed through income-linked or age-linked poverty criteria alone. For these communities, the Rs 1,000 monthly pension represents meaningful support given the very low cash income typical of PVTG livelihoods.

For beneficiaries who are unable to reach a bank due to age, disability, or remote location, the Business Correspondent (Bank Mitra) network in Jharkhand's rural areas can provide doorstep banking services, allowing pension recipients to withdraw their monthly Rs 1,000 from a Bank Mitra near their village. This last-mile financial service delivery is essential to ensure that the Sarvajan Pension reliably and consistently reaches the intended beneficiaries living in Jharkhand's most geographically remote and isolated rural areas.

Advocacy groups and civil society organisations working in Jharkhand have consistently called for an increase in the Sarvajan Pension amount, noting that Rs 1,000 per month does not adequately cover even basic food and medicine costs in the current inflationary environment. The state government has acknowledged these concerns and has indicated that periodic revisions to the pension amount will be considered in future budget allocations, with the long-term goal of eventually reaching a pension amount that genuinely covers basic subsistence needs including food, medicine, and essential utilities for the most economically vulnerable and geographically isolated residents of Jharkhand.

faqs.question: What is Sarvajan Pension Yojana?
faqs.answer: Sarvajan Pension Yojana (SPY) is Jharkhand's social pension scheme that pays Rs 1,000 per month to elderly citizens (60+), widows, destitute women (18+), persons with disabilities (5+), PVTG members, and HIV/AIDS patients who are residents of Jharkhand. The word Sarvajan means 'for all people', reflecting the scheme's broad coverage.

faqs.question: How much pension does Sarvajan Yojana give?
faqs.answer: Rs 1,000 per month per beneficiary, paid by the 5th of every month via DBT (Direct Benefit Transfer) directly to the beneficiary's Aadhaar-linked bank account.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for Sarvajan Pension in Jharkhand?
faqs.answer: Six categories: (1) Senior citizens aged 60+; (2) Widows of any age; (3) Destitute women aged 18+; (4) Persons with 40%+ disability aged 5+; (5) PVTG members of any age; (6) HIV/AIDS patients of any age. All must be permanent residents of Jharkhand.

faqs.question: What is the minimum age for Sarvajan Pension?
faqs.answer:
It depends on the category. For old age pension: 60 years.

For destitute women: 18 years. For persons with disabilities: 5 years.

For widows, PVTG members, and HIV/AIDS patients: there is no minimum age requirement.

faqs.question: Where do I apply for Sarvajan Pension Yojana?
faqs.answer:
Rural applicants should go to the Block Development Officer (BDO) at the block office. Urban applicants should approach the Circle Officer at the circle office.

The application form is available at these offices; there is no fully online application at the state level.

faqs.question: What documents are needed for Sarvajan Pension?
faqs.answer:
Aadhaar card and bank passbook are required for all categories. Additionally: age proof (old age), husband's death certificate (widow), Gram Panchayat destitute certificate (destitute woman), government disability certificate with 40%+ rating (disabled), tribe/PVTG certificate, ART centre certificate (HIV/AIDS).

Jharkhand residency proof is also required.

faqs.question: Is there an income limit for Sarvajan Pension?
faqs.answer:
For widows and destitute women, there is no income ceiling. For the old-age and disability categories, typically the applicant should not have substantial regular income, but the scheme is broadly inclusive and the BDO can assess on a case-by-case basis.

Check with your local BDO for current income limit norms.

faqs.question: Can a disabled child aged 5 years get Sarvajan Pension?
faqs.answer:
Yes. The disability category under Sarvajan Pension has a minimum age of just 5 years, and children aged 5 or older with a certified 40%+ disability can receive Rs 1,000 per month.

The parent or guardian applies on behalf of the child at the BDO or Circle Officer's office.

faqs.question: How long does it take to start receiving Sarvajan Pension?
faqs.answer: After submitting the application, field verification typically takes 2-4 weeks, and complete processing from application to first payment is usually 30-60 days. Once enrolled, the Rs 1,000 arrives by the 5th of the following month.

faqs.question: Can an elderly person receive both central IGNOAPS and Sarvajan Pension?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Many elderly beneficiaries in Jharkhand receive both the central IGNOAPS pension (Rs 200-500/month from NSAP) and the Sarvajan Pension (Rs 1,000/month from Jharkhand state).

The combined monthly pension for an 80+ year old can reach Rs 1,500. Check with your BDO to ensure both components are active.
